from collections import Counter
from math import gcd

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    common = [v for v, _ in counts.most_common(2)]
    marks = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] not in common]
    if not marks:
        return []
    marked_rows = {r for r, c in marks}
    marked_cols = {c for r, c in marks}
    # Marker locations sit at intersections of the regular separator lines.
    # The separator color dominates those rows and columns; the other common
    # color is the tile-interior fill.
    axis_counts = Counter(grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                          if r in marked_rows or c in marked_cols)
    line_color = max(common, key=lambda color: axis_counts[color])
    background = next((color for color in common if color != line_color), line_color)
    rs = sorted(marked_rows)
    cs = sorted(marked_cols)
    dr = dc = 0
    for a, b in zip(rs, rs[1:]): dr = gcd(dr, b-a)
    for a, b in zip(cs, cs[1:]): dc = gcd(dc, b-a)
    if dr == 0: dr = 1
    if dc == 0: dc = 1
    rows = list(range(rs[0], rs[-1]+1, dr))
    cols = list(range(cs[0], cs[-1]+1, dc))
    out = []
    for r1, r2 in zip(rows, rows[1:]):
        row = []
        for c1, c2 in zip(cols, cols[1:]):
            vals = [grid[r1][c1], grid[r1][c2], grid[r2][c1], grid[r2][c2]]
            row.append(vals[0] if vals[0] not in common and all(v == vals[0] for v in vals) else background)
        out.append(row)
    return out
